dream_synopsis: Embry dreams that every attempt to introduce herself becomes a launch update she cannot send, while Maya’s archived laugh loops from a phone with no call button. The dream turns competence into a mask: rockets, folders, classrooms, and voicemails keep offering contact, but only if Embry can choose what stays visible and what disappears.

panels.action: Embry swipes away rows of ordinary messages while pinching one audio file labeled in neutral text; the phone shows no call button, only archive and delete.
panels.mood: controlled uncertainty, private longing, suspended contact
panels.setting: A dark transfer screen floating over a half-formed classroom desk, with message bubbles drifting like files in midair.
panels.shot: Tight foreground close-up on Embry Lawson, face visible and lit by a phone screen; Maya Chen appears as a translucent reflection in the glass, laughing silently.
panels.start_frame_description: Embry’s eyes are fixed on the glowing waveform of Maya’s old voicemail, her thumb hovering between a trash icon and an unlabeled folder; Maya’s smiling reflection flickers over Embry’s cheek.

panels.action: Embry recites three crisp facts about herself, but each sentence appears behind her as a draft message to Maya with the opening line deleted again and again.
panels.mood: self-protective competence, concealed grief, rehearsed restraint
panels.setting: A DOD school classroom that subtly blends into a Yale lab, with name placards, rocket parts, and file folders replacing textbooks.
panels.shot: Medium foreground shot of Embry at a classroom podium, face visible, shoulders squared; Maya sits among indistinct students in the second row, watching without speaking.
panels.start_frame_description: Embry faces forward with a practiced expression, one hand gripping a repaired rocket fin like a note card; behind her, projected text reads and erases: “Maya—” before resetting to blank.

panels.action: Embry aligns the repaired fin and checks launch conditions, then reaches for a send button that transforms into an ignition switch; she stops before pressing it.
panels.mood: longing sharpened by hesitation, technical focus over emotional risk
panels.setting: An impossible launch field inside a phone folder labeled MAYA, with thumbnails of repaired fins forming the horizon.
panels.shot: Foreground three-quarter close-up of Embry kneeling beside a miniature launch rail, face visible; Maya appears beside the rocket as if both memory and teammate, her mouth open in a laugh Embry can hear but not answer.
panels.start_frame_description: Embry’s face is tense and illuminated by the tiny rocket’s indicator light, while Maya’s figure leans in near the fin, bright and unreachable, as if made from the saved voicemail waveform.

panels.action: Embry drags Maya’s voice file, the launch photos, and her self-introduction into separate hidden folders; the countdown reaches one, but instead of launching, the rocket becomes a closed message window.
panels.mood: unresolved preservation, quiet grief, refusal of final confirmation
panels.setting: A suspended dream interface where the classroom, phone transfer, and launch field collapse into a single blank white screen.
panels.shot: Tight frontal foreground shot of Embry, face fully visible, framed by overlapping windows: archive folder, unsent message, classroom roster, and rocket countdown.
panels.start_frame_description: Embry looks directly ahead, jaw set, with Maya visible in two faint panes behind her—one laughing in the voicemail waveform, one waiting beside the unsent message—as Embry’s cursor hovers over save, not send.
